title: fix(app-shell): the Delegated Admin Scope block lists a delegate's companion grants and grants the missing ones (#26191)
body:
Fixes #26191

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

Part of the #26059 ruling (6416233738, Q3 child 5, item 2). UI and docs only: no server change, no spec key.

## What changes

**The Delegated Admin Scope block lists the companion grants a delegate needs.** A scope says what its holder may administer; it does not let the holder in. Once the scope names a business unit (the block's existing gate for its dependent controls), the block lists:

- `setup.access`: enter Setup
- `sys_user`, `sys_business_unit`, `sys_business_unit_member`: read, so the lookups can pick people and units
- `sys_user_position`: create, read, edit and delete, for the assignment rows

Each row is marked "On this set" or "Not on this set", read from the draft being edited (`systemPermissions` and `objects`). A row counts as granted only when every flag it needs is `true`; nothing is inferred.

**"Grant the missing ones" adds only what is missing, as one draft edit.** It is one `setDraft` call, and the set's normal Save persists it. `setup.access` is appended to `systemPermissions`. Each companion object row gains only the flags it lacks. An existing row keeps every key it already has (an extra Edit, a View All), and a row that already covers its grant is left as the same object. Nothing is removed or narrowed, and no new key is written: both keys already exist on `PermissionSetSchema`. The button shows only when the set is writable and something is missing.

**Under a package binding, the hint is shown without the action.** The package door's draft holds, and its Save writes, only the package's own objects (`scopePermissionSet` / `mergePermissionSlice`, ADR-0086 P0). There, the `sys_*` rows would not survive Save, and their absence from the draft says nothing about the stored set. So under a package the block lists the five grants without a granted/missing mark and without the button, plus a note: grant these in Setup, on an environment permission set the delegate holds.

**How the facet knows it is package-bound.** `PermissionAdvancedFacets` gains an optional `packageBound` prop. When the prop is omitted, it is read from `only`. The Studio Access pillar is the one host that sets `only`, and it always edits under a `packageId` (`AccessPillar`'s `packageId` is required). Setup's permission page sets neither. `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` is outside this card's claimed file surface, so this PR does not wire `packageBound={!!packageId}` there. See Acceptance notes.

**Docs.** `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx`: the authoring example now carries `systemPermissions: ['setup.access']`. A new paragraph names the five companion grants and why each is needed, and says the Setup editor lists them and grants the missing ones.

**Strings.** Nine new `perm.admin.companions.*` keys in `metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, in both locales the block's existing strings use (en, zh).

## Tests

`PermissionAdvancedFacets.companionGrants-26191.test.tsx` drives the facet with the draft held as the host holds it. It has 10 cases:

- the five grants are listed and marked missing on an empty set
- grants the set already carries are marked granted, and read alone is not CRUD
- the block is hidden until the scope names a business unit
- one click is one draft write, adds only the missing grants, and leaves existing rows and an unrelated object untouched
- the written set parses under `PermissionSetSchema` and carries no new key
- there is no action when nothing is missing
- read-only: the hint shows and the action does not
- `packageBound`: the hint shows unmarked, there is no action, and the note shows
- the Studio mount (`only`) is package-bound by default
- an explicit `packageBound={false}` keeps the action

Red first, at `c3066c2b` (the test committed, the component not yet changed): 9 failed, 1 passed. The one that passed is the "hidden until a business unit is named" case, which holds both before and after the change. The failures were `Unable to find [data-testid="admin-companions"]` and the like, not errors.

Green, all at head `8ecd7344` (this branch with `main` merged after #26284 landed), from cwd `ui/` under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`:

- `pnpm exec vitest run FILES --maxWorkers=2` over 254 files: every app-shell test file that imports `PermissionAdvancedFacets` or `views/metadata-admin/i18n`, the new file included. `Test Files 254 passed (254)`, `Tests 2578 passed (2578)`. The lock's verdict was `command-exit 0`. The full app-shell suite was not run locally; CI runs it.
- `eslint` on the three changed source files: 0 errors and 5 warnings. Two warnings are new, both `no-explicit-any` in the test harness, where the updater's `prev` is typed `any`, as the prop itself types it. The other three are on existing lines.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: **NOT MEASURED** locally. It ran without the `@object-ui/*` dependency closure built, so it answered only unresolved-module cascades (TS2307 / TS7006). None of them is on a line this PR adds. CI's `Type Check UI` is the reading.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 68 derived commands, reconciled with `--ran` as 66 run (all exit 0) and 2 NOT MEASURED. Both of those are exit-3 prerequisite refusals: `check:skill-examples` (`packages/client-react` was not built; this page's example block carries no type-check marker) and `check:type-check-debt` (it needs the shared lock for its closure build and timed out in the queue). CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs both.
- `node scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs`: exit 0. app-shell has no sdui record, so there was nothing to re-record.

## Acceptance notes

- **Package binding wiring.** The package-bound default is read from `only`, not from `packageId`, because `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` is outside this card's file surface (#26284 held it). Once that file is open to a card, passing `packageBound={!!packageId}` at both facet mounts makes the binding explicit, and the `only` fallback can go. Until then the two coincide by construction: `packageId` is passed only by `AccessPillar`, always together with `studio` chrome, and that chrome is what sets `only`.
- **Marks are exact, not inferred.** A set that reaches Setup through some broader grant is still shown as "Not on this set" for `setup.access`. Clicking then adds the exact capability, which is an addition and narrows nothing.
- `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`, `permission-slice.ts`, the server, `packages/spec` and `ui/packages/i18n` are untouched. app-shell has no sdui record (`node scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs` exits 0).
- The docs path (`content/docs/**`) is not a governed surface: `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --test` over the five files exits 0.
